subject: Pilot extension — calendar days vs. performance slab options
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@aeonhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@aeonhealth.com, Amit Rao <amit.rao@aeonhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot: request to extend calendar window (regulatory hold)

Hi Hannah,

Quick update from our side — the clinical review team flagged an additional privacy assessment that pushed our internal demo window out by ~3 weeks. That leaves us short of the scheduled completion date and our execs are asking whether we can either:

1) extend the pilot by calendar days (3 weeks) with no additional cost, OR
2) convert remaining usage into a token/credit that we can draw down later.

Procurement prefers option (1) because our purchasing window is still blocked for any new commitments. From a product perspective, the team also needs the historical logs used during the demo to remain accessible — would an extension affect log retention or any hosted audit artifacts?

If you could outline the operational implications and a simple amendment we can sign (procurement needs something short), that would be great. We want to avoid pushing more budget requests if possible.

Thanks,
Samira
Director, Data & Clinical Integrations
AeonHealth Solutions

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@aeonhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot: request to extend calendar window (regulatory hold)

Hi Samira — thanks for the heads up and totally understand the procurement constraint. Two practical options from our side: 

A) Calendar extension: we can extend the existing pilot end date by 21 calendar days at no additional usage charge. Conditions: a short operations call (15–20 min) to confirm integration endpoints still function and a one-paragraph addendum (we can email-sign) to update the pilot end date. This preserves logs/audit artifacts as-is for the extended window.

B) Performance slab conversion: if you prefer to keep things contract-light, we can convert the remaining consumption to a performance slab (a rebate-style protection) — effectively a 20% credit on overage usage for a 6-month post-pilot purchase commitment. This requires a commitment signature from procurement.

I'm attaching a brief SOW draft that contains the calendar amendment language and an export of the usage metrics to help you show execs impact. If procurement needs invoice/proration detail, loop in your AP contact and we will show the proforma.

If calendar extension is easiest, reply ACK and I will have legal prepare the single-page amendment. If you want the slab option, Ben (cc) can send the commercial terms.

Best,
Hannah
Head of GTM Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOW_draft_v2.pdf, pilot_metrics_q1.csv

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@aeonhealth.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot: request to extend calendar window (regulatory hold)

Samira — quick commercial note from my side. Hannah covered the two clean options. A couple of alternative mechanics that might fit procurement's preferences: 

• Temporary burst allocation: we can provision a short dedicated burst (10k inference minutes) for the extended window at a 50% discount. That keeps you from hitting throttles while avoiding a long-term commitment.
• Calendar extension + reduced SLA: full calendar extension at no charge, but with a conditional SLA (best-effort - not covered by uptime rebate) during the extra window — useful if internal teams prefer no new invoices.

If you want, I can draft the commercial paragraph that procurement can attach to their PO. Linking the HubSpot deal here for our reference: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/AEON-2026-004.

—Ben
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Samira Khan <samira.k@aeonhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@aeonhealth.com, Amit Rao <amit.rao@aeonhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot: request to extend calendar window (regulatory hold)

Thanks Hannah and Ben — procurement reviewed the options and they prefer the straight calendar extension (Option A). Two clarifying asks before we sign: 

1) Confirmation that the extended days will not change our current audit/log retention policy or make any data accessible to additional parties. We need the same retention window and same access controls.
2) How will this appear on our invoice history? Will you issue an amendment (no charge) or a formal credit memo? Procurement wants a paper trail that shows the pilot amendment and zero net cost.

Procurement contact attached. If you can send over the single-page amendment and a short note for AP, we'll circulate it on Monday.

Samira

Hi Samira / procurement team —

Thanks for confirming the calendar route. Legal has prepared a one-page amendment that simply shifts the pilot end date by 21 calendar days and confirms no change to data retention, access controls, or billing. I have attached the amendment template and will send it via DocuSign this morning so you have an auditable acceptance flow for AP.

Next steps (quick):
1) I will send the DocuSign link to procure@aeonhealth.com (you will get an email shortly).
2) Once signed, we will update the pilot end date in our system and keep logs/audit artifacts unchanged.
3) Operations will schedule a 15-min health check for Tue 4/14 — Hannah will coordinate.
